News.title: Russian missiles flying near Chernobyl plant risking ‘major accident’ 40 years after nuclear catastrophe, Ukraine says
News.content:
RUSSIAN missiles flying near to the Chernobyl nuclear plant are risking a “major accident”, Ukraine says.

A top state prosecutor claimed Russia has repeatedly piloted missiles and drones near the disused nuclear facility during waves of brutal attacks on Ukraine.





General Ruslan Kravchenko detailed previously unreported Russian military activity near the site as Ukraine prepares to mark the 40th anniversary of the 1986 disaster on Sunday.

Alongside Chernobyl, Ukraine is home to four nuclear power plants.

This includes Zaporizhzhia — Europe‘s largest – which has been under Russian control since the start of the invasion in 2022.

Both the Chernobyl and the Khmelnytskyi nuclear plant in western Ukraine have been on the flight path of Russian missiles, said Kravchenko.

As many as 35 Kinzhal missiles have been detected within 20km of either Chernobyl or the Khmelnytskyi sites.

Worse still, 18 of those missiles passed within 20km of both locations on the same flight.

“Such launches cannot be explained by any military considerations,” Kravchenko said.



“It is evident that the flights over the nuclear facilities are carried out solely for the purpose of intimidation or terror.”

In February last year, an object identified as a long-range Russian attack drone struck the facility, penetrating the radiation containment shield.

The Kremlin denied any involvement at the time, stating its forces do not target nuclear infrastructure.

Instead, it claimed Ukraine had carried out the attack themselves as a “provocation”.

More recently, Kravchenko said that Kinzhal missiles had fallen to the ground on three separate occasions.



The air-launched hypersonic missile that can carry a 500kg warhead landed within 10km of the Khmelnytskyi plant.

It remains unclear why the missiles came down, but Kravchenko said the wreckage did not suggest they were intercepted.

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said it has “deep concern” about military activity in the vicinity of nuclear power plants.



The last of Chernobyl’s reactors was decommissioned in 2000 and the Zone Of Alienation around the plant has since become a popular tourist attraction.

In total, around 650,000 men volunteered to help contain the nuclear fallout when it happened.

Russian scientists estimate that up to 125,000 had died by 2005, but authorities deny a definite link between the number of fatalities and radiation exposure.

What happened at Chernobyl? WHEN an alarm bellowed out at the nuclear plant on April 26, 1986, workers looked on in horror as the control panels signaled a major meltdown in the number four reactor. The safety switches had been switched off in the early hours to test the turbine but the reactor overheated and generated a blast – the equivalent of 500 nuclear bombs. The reactor’s roof was blown off and a plume of radioactive material was blasted into the atmosphere. As air was sucked into the shattered reactor, it ignited flammable carbon monoxide gas causing a fire which burned for nine days. The catastrophe released at least 100 times more radiation than the atom bombs dropped on Nagasaki and Hiroshima. Soviet authorities waited 24 hours before evacuating the nearby town of Pripyat – giving the 50,000 residents just three hours to leave their homes. After the accident traces of radioactive deposits were found in Belarus where poisonous rain damaged plants and caused animal mutations. But the devastating impact was also felt in Scandinavia, Switzerland, Greece, Italy, France and the UK. An 18-mile radius known as the “Exclusion Zone” was set up around the reactor following the disaster. Most recently, on February 24, 2022 during the Russian invasion, Ukraine lost control over the Chernobyl site.

Petro Hurin, 76, is one of the few of liquidators still alive to this day.

He said his health was never the same after he was dispatched to the scene of the disaster.

He and 39 other workers were sent into the nuclear facility just a month after the explosion – today only five survive.

Petro said not a single worker who went to Chernobyl was ever in good health again.

News.title: Watch as giant tortoise is fitted with custom WHEELS by vets after struggling to walk
News.content:
THIS is the moment a giant tortoise walks again using an ingenious invention after struggling to move.

An Aldabra giant tortoise has been given a new lease of life after a genius vet fitted it with its very own set of custom wheels.





The tortoise had been struggling to move, with severe weakness in its back legs forcing it to drag itself along the ground.

It was a heartbreaking sight for his keepers, who knew they had to do something fast.

They rushed the giant creature in for urgent, specialist treatment.

Veterinarians carried out a full examination to get to the bottom of the mystery.

They feared the worst, but X-rays luckily showed no fractures or dislocations.

Experts believe the injury was likely caused by trauma, potentially during a scrap with other tortoises.

Dr Nielsen B Donato designed custom-made wheeled support to take the weight off the tortoise’s hind legs.

The innovative device allows the creature to move about far more freely.



A video of the amazing transformation was shared on April 8 and has since gone viral.

It has already racked up more than 100,000 likes and thousands of comments.

Dr Donato revealed the magic moment the tortoise was placed back on the ground, it began moving again with total ease.

He said he felt proud of both himself and his team as they watched it glide around the lab for the first time.

The tortoise is now back home continuing its recovery outdoors.



Getting back into the fresh air is key for the species to soak up the natural sunlight.

The vet says further treatment, such as laser therapy, could be used if needed to help bring down any inflammation.

The heartwarming procedure took place at a hospital in Taguig City, Philippines.

Fans online were quick to poke fun at the new set of wheels.

One joked: “After this, he will no longer be on turtle pace.”



Another quipped: “They see me rollin’. They hatin’.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A third viewer added: “Amazing. Feel like the wheels are a little too tall but what do I know.”

And a fourth laughed: “I am imagining one gets locked and the tortoise is just going around in circles. I shouldn’t laugh… Glad the tortoise is getting the care he needs though!”

News.title: Photos of pets outnumber snaps of family & partners on phones, survey reveals
News.content:
THE average pet owner’s phone has 20 per cent more pictures of cats, dogs and other beloved animals – than their partners or dearest friends and family.

A poll of 2,000 with furry companions revealed they store an average of 176 snaps of four-legged friends on their device, compared to 147 pictures of their other half.





Pets also outnumber other loved ones, with respondents storing just 65 photos of their parents and 57 of their best friends on average.

It comes as 46 per cent of pet parents consider taking photos of something as a way of showing their love for it, with 40 per cent agreeing that a camera roll is a strong indicator of who or what people value the most.

Looking back on their camera roll makes more than half happy (51 per cent), while others feel nostalgic (36 per cent) and warm (33 per cent).

In fact, in the last month alone, 20 new pictures of pets have been added to camera rolls as 14 per cent snap pictures every single day – with these keen photographers taking around five photos daily.

Nearly seven in 10 (69 per cent) pet photographers added they are now using AI features or filters on their device to enhance pictures of their pets.

The research was commissioned by Samsung to celebrate the launch of the Galaxy A57 5G, which has Awesome Intelligence and ‘Fun Mode’ camera features that lets users use AR lenses to transform into different characters such as a pug or cat.

It also emerged Millennials have the most pet pictures on their phones, averaging 217 images, followed by Gen Z with 204, while Boomers trail behind on 103 snaps.

But overall, 52 per cent see their pet as a central member of the family, making them worthy of documenting at every opportunity.



When a pet is playing is the most likely moment to turn into a mini photoshoot (62 per cent), although 56 per cent can’t resist snapping a picture when their furry friend is fast asleep.

Despite 68 per cent preferring candid shots of their pet behaving naturally, 70 per cent still reach for their phone when their pet is doing something unusual or unexpected.

For nearly a quarter (23 per cent), these photos don’t just stay on their camera roll, with owners regularly sharing them on social media. And 48 per cent noticed pet pictures get more engagement than any other content they post.

News.title: Horror moment fairground reveller films as ride collapses after cables snap sending screaming revellers plummeting
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a fairground ride suddenly collapses mid-air sending riders plunging to the ground.

Dramatic video — taken by a passenger on the ride — captured the exact second the cables snap in the horror malfunction which left 11 people injured.





The phone camera footage begins with people laughing and enjoying the ride, which has passengers buckled into swing seats being swung in a circle.

Suddenly, all the seats crash to the ground as a loud mechanical sound can be heard and passengers scream.

Later, passengers can be seen lying on the floor of the platformed ride as they wait for medical attention.

Emergency services raced to the scene at Parque Las Vegas in Guaíba, southern Brazil, on Sunday 19 April, treating adults as well as children and teenagers.

Among those on board was Jeniffer Ferreira, 26, who escaped with minor injuries. She was taken to hospital and later discharged.

Her boyfriend, 28, suffered a fractured vertebra.

He was transferred to Hospital Cristo Redentor in nearby Porto Alegre but was also released the following day.



According to the fire department, the collapse happened after part of the structure – known as the tower – broke during the ride’s ascent.

One teenager who witnessed the incident said the attraction had been making “strange noises” moments before the collapse.

Investigators later found that two of the ride’s support cables had snapped, although it remains unclear if this directly caused the failure.

Police have also raised concerns over a lack of maintenance records, suggesting the equipment may have been in a “very precarious” condition.

The park, which had only opened in the city on March 14 and was due to run until April 26, was immediately shut down.



In a statement, Parque Las Vegas said it “deeply regrets” what happened and is assisting victims and their families, insisting it complies with all safety regulations.

The attraction had been operating in the car park of a Havan store, though the retailer stressed it has no connection to the park and that it operates independently.

Local authorities confirmed the site had the necessary permits but said operations have been suspended as a precaution while the investigation continues.

News.title: Evil foster mum allowed her son to rape me & film abuse from the age of 5… there was a shocking reason she walked free
News.content:
COWERING in bed, Amanda Brown sobbed as she heard the door open again. The little girl, who had been taken away from her mother at just six months old, was being abused by her evil foster family.

The Robertsons subjected her and other children in their care to years of physical, sexual and mental abuse. Now, after 30 years, Amanda has finally faced her abusers in court. Bravely waving her anonymity, she tells the Sun the horror of her ordeal, and why the outcome of her court case is ‘disgusting’ and ‘disappointing’.



Amanda, now 38, went into the care of Jennifer Robertson, now 79, when she was just six months old, after social services took her away from her biological mother.

She lived with the Robertsons until the age of five, and during that time suffered a string of physical assaults from Jennifer, whilst her son Steven, now 52, and her late husband sexually assaulted and raped her.

The mother and son were both sentenced at the High Court in Edinburgh this week, but Jennifer avoided jail time, which Amanda says is “not justice at all”.



“All I ever knew was abuse, at the time I thought it was normal,” Amanda tells the Sun.

I don’t know how we survived. Jennifer knew that he was doing this to me

“I just thought it happened to everybody. Steven would sexually assault me and another victim to perform with me – it was to the point I was bleeding.

“It was a repeated cycle of Steven coming to my bedroom at night. I don’t remember a day when I wasn’t getting hurt.

“Looking back on it now, I don’t know how we survived. Jennifer knew that he was doing this to me.”

Amanda says Jennifer would also punch her in the stomach and hold her head under the water during bathtime to stop her from breathing.



During the same time period, her son Steven preyed on her by repeatedly kissing her on the mouth, chest and private parts.

In one particularly evil act, he induced her to commit a sex act on him and another youngster.

“I just feel like they only stole my childhood; they’ve stolen these years trying to get justice. I just want to be able to live.”

“This has been my whole life.”

When she got to the Robertsons’ house in Murthly, Perthshire, Scotland, Steven was a teenager.



Amanda says she does not know when the abuse began, as she was a baby when she went into their household.

Steven targeted girls who had been placed in his mother’s care at the family home.

He sexually assaulted Amanda while acting with his now deceased father, Alan Robertson, in the 1980s and 1990s.

All the children were under the age of five when he began abusing them.



“I never said stop,” Amanda adds in tears.

“I just stood there and cried, and at the end, I would be told to clean myself up, and an older sibling who lived in the property would clean me up.

“It was painful, I can remember the pain to this day. It was excruciating, and that pain affected me right through my life.

“Steven’s assaults were filmed on his VHS camera. I was under the impression that he would hand these out to people. So I never felt at ease to speak out.”

‘It was like hell, a house of horrors’

Living in the house was “like hell” to Amanda, who said there was “no love” in the family.



Her foster mother, Jennifer, subjected the children to cruel and unnatural treatment, which included forcing some children to wear urine-soaked underwear on their heads and to sit in cold baths.

“My flashbacks are only of the punishments of being forced to eat beans, she would punch me, and there was one incident where she held me under the water, and she kept pushing me back and forth into the water,”

“The house was like I was in hell, there was nowhere I could turn to in that house and feel like you were safe.



“When I see my children, I light up, and I’m excited to give them a cuddle; it was not like that.

“You’d be assaulted, there was a lack of food, and there was no safe space there.”

Jennifer was found guilty of verbally and physically abusing three children, and of failing to take steps to prevent the assault and sexual abuse of another child by her son.

Amanda explained that at the age of five, the process of her being adopted began, but Jennifer and Steven were still involved in her life.

She says: “I had to go back to their house because the three years of paperwork of adoption had not been finalised.



‘My adoptive parents saved my life’

“My adoptive parents felt they were under threat because she would say I would go back to adoption.

“My adoptive family felt straight away that something wasn’t right.

“I’d walk into the door, and Jennifer would punch me straight in the stomach.

“My adoptive family were coming up to pick me up, and my hair was a mess, and my clothes weren’t done properly.”

Amanda claims that when the paperwork was finally completed, her adoptive mum took her to the police, and it was found that she had internal damage.



“It took me a year to disclose everything to my adoptive family. I didn’t really trust the police, so I didn’t say much to them.

“After coming to me, three weeks after they stopped investigating.

“I felt like I was not being heard by the police. I felt like if I said something, I’d be in trouble.



“It was only when I got adopted that I was like ‘why aren’t you hurting me?’ To me, it was normal. My adoptive parents saved my life.

“They did everything in their power to stand beside me to make sure my voice got heard. I could not have wished for a better family.

“I stayed with them from 8 until I was 16. To this day, I class them as my mum and dad.”

Last week, Steven Robertson was jailed for 11 years with a further three-year sentence extension during which time he will be subject to close monitoring and supervision.

His name has been added to the sex offenders register indefinitely.



‘It wasn’t a fair outcome – it’s disgusting’

Jennifer Robertson was given a Community Payback Order with conduct requirements and ordered to perform 250 hours of unpaid work within 12 months.

Judge John Morris KC said: “It is clear that your victims have suffered severe harm and continue to suffer severe trauma.

“You have a complete lack of remorse even for the things you admit doing.”

Sentencing Jennifer Robertson, he acknowledged her age, that she’s a fall risk and added: “I am well aware that your victims want you to go to prison.

“However, I am narrowly persuaded to draw back from sending you to prison. I am persuaded in the circumstances that I can draw back from custody and to impose a community payback order.



“Such a sentence is a direct alternative to custody. It is designed to be an onerous sentence.

“Should you not comply with any part of the sentence, you will be brought back before me and you can be sent to prison.”

Non-harassment orders, banning both individuals from contacting or attempting to contact the victims, were also granted indefinitely.

Victims were seen shouting and crying in the courtroom when Jennifer’s sentencing was given.

Amanda says she felt “let down” that Jennifer did not get jail time.



She is just going to be living her life as norma

“I don’t think it was a fair outcome. For her to walk away freely is just disgusting.

“We relieved everything, and where has this really got us? I just feel disappointed.

“Towards Steven, I feel like I had some sort of justice, but with Jennifer, it doesn’t feel like it.

“She is just going to be living her life as normal. I don’t think her age should be taken into consideration; she didn’t care about our ages at the time of the abuse.”

In 2018, the Scottish Police came to her house following abuse claims related to Jennifer and Steven.



“In my heart, I knew that someone had spoken up, and if I had the choice to relieve this, I wouldn’t have chosen to, but I knew who it was and that needed help.”

Jennifer and Steven Robertson were found guilty of a total of nine charges on March 20.

The Crown led evidence from the victims, who gave consistent accounts describing a pattern of offending behaviour by Jennifer.



Amanda said the abuse affected her self-worth and that for a long time, she never valued herself.

“I just allowed men to take what they wanted from me because I didn’t feel like I was worthy of love,” she said.

I can honestly say that if it hadn’t been for my children, I wouldn’t be here today

“Throughout my life growing up, I just never had a voice. That was taken from me at such a young age.

“It’s always been so chaotic because I spent so long trying to be heard, and the last seven years, this has come back again.

“While trying to support my family, I also had to fight this battle. It’s been a journey on its own.”



Amanda’s children, aged four to 20 years old, are her “reason for living”, she said.

“I can honestly say that if it hadn’t been for my children, I wouldn’t be here today.

“When I was older, and I struggled to cope in my teens, I used to drink a lot.

“Now I want to be able to move forward. I want my children and myself to have the best life.

“I feel like now my voice has been heard, I can settle down.”



Police Scotland’s Detective Constable Ursula Honeyman says: “Jennifer Robertson had a duty of care to these children.

“She not only neglected them but did nothing when her son sexually abused them.

“Steven Robertson systematically abused young girls staying at his family home over a number of years and now faces the consequences of his depraved actions.”

Faye Cook, Procurator Fiscal for High Court Sexual Offences, says:

“Jennifer Robertson had a clear duty to protect the young people in her care and to keep them safe as an approved foster carer.

“Instead, she caused profound harm through sustained cruelty and abuse, including enabling others to sexually abuse the children.



“Steven Robertson’s predatory behaviour went unchecked, allowing him to systematically abuse and rape these young girls over a number of years.

“Their actions have had lifelong consequences for those affected, and I am grateful to the survivors for the courage they have shown throughout the prosecution process.”

News.title: Hawaii tourist charged with attempted murder after ‘stabbing veteran boat captain’ on dream tour
News.content:
SNORKEL SHOCK Hawaii tourist charged with attempted murder after ‘stabbing veteran boat captain’ on dream tour

A HAWAII snorkel trip turned into a blood-soaked nightmare after a tourist allegedly stabbed a veteran boat captain mid-tour.

A 21-year-old man from Kansas is accused of launching the frenzied attack with a filet knife during a three-hour excursion off the coast of the Big Island.





Cops said that Avery Nissen, of Overland Park, has been charged with second-degree attempted murder, first-degree assault, and second-degree assault.

The horror unfolded on Thursday afternoon as the boat returned to Honokōhau Harbor in Kailua-Kona.

Cops say Nissen allegedly turned on 62-year-old captain Stanley Lurbiecki, a long-time figure in the boating industry, stabbing him multiple times.

According to local outlet KHNL, Lurbiecki suffered stab wounds to his head, hands and lower abdomen.

Read more Hawaii news FLASH FLOOD Hundreds rescued from catastrophic flooding as fears rise of imminent dam burst

He was rushed to hospital and is now in a stable condition.

Terrified passengers reportedly stepped in to restrain Nissen after the alleged attack, preventing further injuries.

Police said officers were called at around 3.21pm to reports of a stabbing on a boat returning from sea.

Investigators say the suspect and victim were both onboard a catamaran owned by tour company Hawaii Nautical.



The motive for the alleged attack remains unknown.

Mark Towill, owner and president of Hawaii Nautical, told KHNL: “Stan is stable, he’s recovering. He’s a real hero and a fighter.”

“I’m just incredibly grateful that our team is safe and that the situation ended the way it did,” Towill said.

“I’ve never heard of anything like this happening in this industry before, and just really grateful to all of our team for the way that they reacted, the professionalism that was demonstrated.”

Nissen is being held in a Hawaii jail on a $1.57 million bond.



He appeared in court on Monday, with his next hearing scheduled for June 17.

News.title: Prince Harry’s quiet but touching gesture to his grandmother The Queen on her 100th birthday revealed
News.content:
HARRY'S TRIBUTE Prince Harry’s quiet but touching gesture to his grandmother The Queen on her 100th birthday revealed

PRINCE Harry honoured his grandmother, the late Queen Elizabeth II, with a quiet but touching gesture this week.

As senior members of the royal family chose to celebrate what would have been the late Queen’s 100th birthday more publicly, The Duke of Sussex opted for a more subtle but sweet gesture.





From thousands of miles away in Montecito, California, Prince Harry arranged for flowers to be placed at St George’s Chapel in Windsor, according to Hello.

The site is of significance since it’s where his grandmother was laid to rest in September 2022.

For Harry, it’s not the first time he has quietly honoured the late Queen in this way though.

When he was in the UK he privately paid his respects at the chapel, followed by another visit in 2025, which marked the third anniversary of her passing.

The King George VI Memorial Chapel is also where other royals including King George VI and Queen Elizabeth, the Queen Mother, her husband Prince Philip, and her sister Princess Margaret were laid to rest, making it even more significant for Harry.

Prince Harry‘s close relationship with his grandmother is one that is undeniable – Harry and Meghan even honoured the monarch by naming their daughter Lilibet, which was her childhood nickname

After his grandmother’s death Harry recalled several memories and shared: “I cherish these times shared with you… You are already sorely missed, not just by us, but by the world over.”

Then in his controversial memoir, Spare, Harry described his final phone call with his beloved grandmother, which touched on topics ranging from the British weather to her health.



Speaking of learning of her death during a flight to Balmoral, he said: “I spent much of the flight staring at the clouds, replaying the last time I’d spoken with Granny.”

Prince Philip’s friend Gyles Brandreth previously gave an insight into the late monarch’s relationship with the Duke of Sussex.

An excerpt of the book, published in The Mail On Sunday says: “I know she was anxious that Harry should ‘find his feet’ in California and ‘find really useful things to do’.

“The Queen was devoted to Harry. She loved him, she thought him ‘huge fun’, and she truly wished him well in his new life abroad.

“Whenever Harry called his grandmother from Montecito, he was always put through to Her Majesty immediately.”



It was also revealed the Queen secretly fought painful cancer in the final year of her life.

Her late Majesty is said to have had a form of bone marrow cancer, which symptoms include bone pain, before her death.

Her death certificate officially recorded her cause of death as “old age”.

Meanwhile, in the London, royals gathered for a family photograph in a display of unity and in memory of the late Queen.

King Charles, 77, then threw a palace bash for 190 special guests where he presented cards and led a rendition of ‘Happy Birthday’ to three centenarians to celebrate the occasion.



The three special guests – who all shared her birthday – were invited to the palace and received a warm welcome from the King, Queen, Kate and William.

Charles personally gave three 100-year-olds their special cards signed by himself and Queen Camilla.

The King, in a video message, also paid a heartfelt tribute to his “darling Mama”, but said much of life today would likely have “troubled her deeply”.

He said he took heart from her belief that “goodness will prevail” and that a “brighter dawn is never far from the horizon”, and said the milestone anniversary should be celebrated as a “life well-lived” rather than marking an “absence”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The late Queen had two birthday celebrations each year – one on her actual birth date and the other on her “official” birthday.



The latter was a public celebration and marked by public gun salutes in places like Windsor Great Park, the Tower of London and Hyde Park.

News.title: Fury as Travellers take over beauty spot for 2 months leaving mounds of ‘rubbish & human POO near children’s play area’
News.content:
HUMAN faeces, ferocious dogs and a site resembling a tip is what residents near a beauty spot are having to endure from people living on an illegal Travellers site.

For the last two months, residents around Highridge Common on the outskirts of Bristol have had to endure nights of incessant dog barking, loud music and an unsightly mess on what was a popular play area.





But for one local mother, who didn’t want to be named, the final straw came when she found human poo on the common where youngsters used to play.

She said: “It has now become too much for many who live around here. I like to think I’m tolerant about those wanting to live a different lifestyle, but human waste is the last straw.

“I’ve got two children under 12 and I can’t allow them to go over there and play. It’s not just the human waste but there are some dogs which look decidedly unfriendly.”

Bristol City Councillor for the ward of Bishopsworth, Richard Eddy, said there has been a litany of complaints since the Travellers arrived on the site at the end of February.

He said: “I’ve had to deal with reports of human waste found near children’s play areas on the site as well as soiled nappies, late night music and barking dogs.

“People shouldn’t have to put up with this level of anti-social behaviour. I have council taxpayers telling me, ‘I shouldn’t have to foot the bill to clean up the mess these people create’.

“And I can’t argue with their point of view. Not only is it the cost of cleaning up but there is a significant legal cost in getting these people off the land.



“We are footing a bill which local people shouldn’t be asked to pay and that is wrong.

“I have been a councillor for a third of a century and the city council has won a national reputation in that time for being a soft touch for tackling Travellers.

“The site is now a complete eyesore and local residents want an end to what they see as inexcusable – and I agree with them.”

Another resident, too scared at being identified for fear of reprisals, said local people are fed up with the situation.

The 39-year-old care worker said: “You only have to take a look at the place to realise these people don’t have any responsibilities about keeping the site clean and tidy.



“We have old cookers, furniture, garden waste and who knows what just littering what used to be pleasant play area.

“This shouldn’t be allowed to happen and Bristol seems to be a place a lot of Travellers gravitate to the area because they know that the council takes a softly-softly approach to evicting them.”

But following a large number of complaints, Bristol City Council were forced to act after the group set themselves up on the common on the edge of Bishopsworth on the last day of February.



A council spokesperson said the authority had taken the rare decision to evict the encampment due to the volume of objections it had received from the public.

He said: “We are aware of the group of travellers currently parked on Highridge Common.

“The group has been there around seven weeks and we carried out a full welfare assessment when they arrived and offered them support and advice.

“Due to a large number of complaints, the location of the group and the length of time they have been on the site, we have taken the decision to take legal action to evict the group from the site.

“It is uncommon for us to have to take this sort of action, as we maintain a good relationship with the Travelling community. Traveller encampments pass through Bristol every year, and the majority of them cause very little disruption and raise few complaints.



“An eviction of this nature is a last resort and not a decision we take lightly, but we will take action when an encampment starts to have an adverse impact on neighbouring homes.

“Our priority is to support ethnic Gypsy and Traveller communities onto full time permanent sites.”

Bristol City Council started the legal repossession process to evict the Travellers on March 19.

News.title: Jodie Marsh WINS major court battle to keep nine monkeys at her Essex rescue centre
News.content:
Jodie Marsh WINS major court battle to keep nine monkeys at her Essex rescue centre

Marsh took Uttlesford District Council to court after being refused a wild animal licence, but she has now been given approval to keep 12 marmosets at her rescue centre in Essex

View 4 Images Jodie Marsh runs an animal sanctuary at Fripps Farm, Essex, after her career as a glamour model (Image: LDRS)

Former glamour model Jodie Marsh has been granted a new license to keep monkeys after a drawn-out legal battle.

The 47-year-old has been given the green light to keep 12 marmosets at her rescue centre at Fripps Farm in Lindsell, near Great Dunmow, Essex. Marsh took Uttlesford District Council to court after it previously refused to grant a wild animal licence, meaning she could not legally adopt eight ring-tailed lemurs, but she won her case in June.

She said she was "elated" and "completely over the moon" after Uttlesford District Council approved her latest application. She told the BBC: "I knew we would get the licence because we'd done everything correctly. With the new primate law coming into effect, many people won't be able to keep their marmosets, and thousands will need homes. It is so crucial that those of us who can, do have the licence, so we can rescue more if needed."

View 4 Images Marsh's Fripps Farm has been at the centre of a protracted legal battle to secure a licence to keep monkeys (Image: James Linsell Clark / SWNS)

The Animal Welfare (Primate Licences) (England) Regulations 2024 introduced a licensing regime to protect the welfare of primates kept in England. The council confirmed that Marsh's primate licence was effective from April 6, until April 5 2029. She said the new regulations were "higher than zoo standards" and feared many small monkeys would be put down or abandoned if their owners were unable to get a new licence.

View 4 Images Jodie Marsh was previously reported to RSPCA for 'animal abuse' (Image: Instagram/ @jodiemarshtv)

Marsh rose to fame in the ITV series Essex Wives in 2002 and became a regular face in the tabloid newspapers. Alpacas, emus and reptiles are among the animals she keeps at the private 3.5-acre (1.4-hectare) Fripps Farm, which she founded in 2020 and used OnlyFans to partly fund.

View 4 Images Last week Marsh appeared Chelmsford Magistrates' Court accused of assaulting a man at the farm in January (Image: Sam Russell/PA Wire)

Article continues below

Last week Marsh appeared at Chelmsford Magistrates' Court accused of assaulting a man at the farm in January. She is alleged to have grabbed Christopher Hynes by the neck at the animal sanctuary she runs. She appeared at Chelmsford magistrates' court on Friday where she denied assault and using threatening and abusive words against Mr Hynes and Susan Hammond.

Marsh was bailed and will face trial in May next year.

News.title: Defiant Keir Starmer lashes out at critics calling on him to quit at bad-tempered PMQs
News.content:
Defiant Keir Starmer lashes out at critics calling on him to quit at bad-tempered PMQs

Keir Starmer shot back as he was asked by Kemi Badenoch and Green MP Dr Ellie Chowns if he was going to resign over the Peter Mandelson scandal - accusing the Tory leader of being 'wrong, wrong, wrong'

PMQs: Keir Starmer defiant as Badenoch calls for his resignation

Defiant Keir Starmer came swinging for critics who demanded he steps down over the Peter Mandelson scandal.

‌



He lashed out at Tory leader Kemi Badenoch and Green MP Dr Ellie Chowns after they called for him to quit - saying his focus was on delivering for the country.

‌



The Prime Minister is under growing pressure after sacking Foreign Office chief Sir Olly Robbins following revelations about Mandelson's vetting. In a tense exchange at PMQs, Mrs Badenoch said the PM must "finally take responsibility and go".

‌



View 2 Images Keir Starmer shot back at his critics as he faced criticism over the Mandelson scandal (Image: House of Commons/UK Parliament/PA Wire)

Mr Starmer shot back that Mrs Badenoch had been "wrong, wrong, wrong" since the revelation that UK Security Vetting (UKSV) recommended against clearing Mandelson before he was sent to Washington.

The PM said: "Mr Speaker, the leader of the opposition claimed on Friday that Mandelson could not have been cleared against security advice. She was wrong about that.

‌



"She said that ministers must have been told she was wrong about that. She claimed there was deliberate dishonesty. She was wrong about that. Wrong, wrong, wrong.

"She rushed to judgment, as she always did, just like the Iran war. Mr Speaker, I was elected by the British people because they let the country down for 14 long years.

View 2 Images Kemi Badenoch called on the PM to 'take responsibility' (Image: House of Commons/UK Parliament/PA Wire)

‌



"Whatever she says, whatever noise they make, nothing is going to distract me from delivering for our country."

Mr Starmer has faced questions after previously telling the Commons that due process was followed over Mandelson's appointment. It has since become clear that he was not informed of UKSV's recommendation - but in an explosive evidence session on Tuesday Sir Olly said he was right not pass the information on.

In a furious exchange, the Tory leader had said: "Mr Speaker, I cannot accuse the Prime Minister of deliberately misleading the House, but everyone can see what has happened here. This was not due proces, everyone knows the price of misleading the house. Will the Prime Minister finally take responsibility and go."

‌



Speaking to the Foreign Affairs Committee on Tuesday, Sir Olly claimed No10 had shown a "dismissive" attitude to Mandelson's vetting. Dr Chowns told the Commons: "The Prime Minister appointed Mandelson in a desperate and doomed attempt to pander to Donald Trump, despite knowing about his friendship with the paedophile Epstein and his links to foreign states.

"The Prime Minister resisted and then took a dismissive and extraordinarily incurious attitude to vetting, compromising national security. And now he's throwing the civil servant under the bus to save his own skin.

"All this from a Prime Minister who pledged to restore trust and integrity in government, but who has repeatedly betrayed the trust of voters and let the country down. Does the Prime Minister not recognise that the best thing he can do to restore trust and integrity is to take true responsibility and resign?"

Article continues below

Mr Starmer responded: "Let me just correct what she said. There was no dismissive attitude to developed vetting. I knew the post was subject to developed vetting.

"What didn't happen was I was told of the UKSV recommendation. That was a serious error of judgment. Had I been told the appointment wouldn't have gone ahead."

News.title: Should St George's day be a bank holiday? Take our poll and have your say
News.content:
Should St George's day be a bank holiday? Take our poll and have your say

The UK has several different national holidays, none of which have been given Bank Holiday status by the Government, but many Britons would have that change

View 3 Images St George's Day has been celebrated for centuries, but it isn't a Bank Holiday (Image: ANDY RAIN/EPA/Shutterstock)

St George's Day will see Brits living in England celebrate the national day this Thursday, reigniting a longtime debate about its status in the Bank Holiday schedule.

‌



The April 23 occasion marks the death of St George, the Christian martyr and English patron saint who was canonised for his refusal to denounce his religion and immortalised for heroically slaying a dragon. While being a national day for England, it has never been given Bank Holiday status - despite massive public demand.

‌



The Government this week poured cold water on the accelerating demand for another day off, stating there were "no plans" to do so due to the massive potential financial costs.

‌



View 3 Images St George was made a martyr for refusing to denounce his faith (Image: Getty Images)

Speaking to the Express, the spokesperson said even a one-off additional Bank holiday - not unlike the one allowed for the King's 2023 Coronation - would cost the Government up to £2 billion". They said: "While we are proud to celebrate all of our patron saints, the current pattern of bank and public holidays is well established, and we have no plans to change it."

‌



If the above link doesn't work for you, please click here to have your say on whether the occasion should be made a Bank Holiday.

St George's Day has been celebrated as a major national holiday since as early as the 9th century, and debated across the UK for decades. Two new petitions calling on the Government to make it a Bank Holiday have come and gone in 2026 so far, and at one point they both ran concurrently.

The primary petition of the two, which was closed in March, called for the Bank Holiday in line with other countries who provide public days off for national days.

‌



View 3 Images Campaigns have long sought to add St George's Day to the country's list of Bank Holidays (Image: Guy Bell/Shutterstock)

Proclaiming "England should be proud of St George’s Day", the petition, which was signed by hundreds of people, stated: "We feel the Government should review England’s national holidays and that England should not be penalised. We feel that England, as a nation, should be able to celebrate their nation’s day.

"We feel that England should show more support towards this special day by making it a Bank Holiday so people can get together as a community and celebrate. We believe England should no longer be underprivileged."

Article continues below

Dozens of countries around the world have Bank Holidays to celebrate major national days, many being former British Empire colonies that won their independence. In Europe, France, Germany, Italy, and the Netherlands celebrate theirs, which are associated with unity, becoming a republic and celebrating the monarchy, between April and October.

The UK, as a united group of four nations, has several different national days, Wales has St David's Day on March 1, and Scotland has St Andrew's Day on November 30. However, none of these are celebrated as Bank Holidays.

News.title: MSE alert as new Amazon and eBay payment option 'could cost you'
News.content:
MSE alert as new Amazon and eBay payment option 'could cost you'

Specialists warned shoppers that this new feature might save time, but it all comes at a price

View 3 Images Paying this way online may cause issues if something goes wrong with the purchase (stock image) (Image: Getty)

Shoppers are being urged to "think twice" before choosing a convenient option when making any big online purchases. Despite saving time, this payment feature could quietly strip shoppers of vital consumer protection rights should anything go wrong later .

‌



Pay by Bank has been offered on platforms such as Amazon and eBay, offering a faster checkout without reaching for a bank card. However, if issues arise later, shoppers may discover they don't have the same protections that are ordinarily a legal requirement.

‌



An MSE spokesperson said: "Don't use this new Pay by Bank option on Amazon, eBay, or elsewhere until you've watched this video. Pay by bank is a quicker, easier way to complete a normal bank transfer, but you lose vital purchase protections you normally get when paying on plastic.

‌



"These are Section 75 on credit cards and chargeback on credit and debit cards. Both of these give you an extra way to try getting your money back if something goes wrong and the retailer is not playing ball."

The personal finance team advises that, for any "big important purchase", it would be "safest to stick with cards", reports the Express.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



What is 'Pay by Bank'?

The Pay by Bank feature is essentially a much faster way to complete transactions when shopping online at certain retailers. The process is quicker because it does not require the shopper to enter any card or account details, operating entirely via a bank transfer.

It's due to this 'transfer' rather than a transaction difference that customers may unknowingly be surrendering crucial protections against delivery or product issues. MSE founder Martin Lewis previously said online in 2025: "Ultimately, it's just a bank transfer, which means you don't get the same refund rights, like chargeback or Section 75, if things go wrong that you do when you pay by card. So for small things it's no biggie, but beware with big, important transactions."

The MSE website outlined how the Pay by Bank process typically works:

‌



You pick your bank from a list You get sent to your bank's app or online banking to log in (using your fingerprint, face, PIN or password) Your bank shows the pre-filled details of the payment (including the amount and recipient) You approve the payment through your bank and get sent back to where you started for confirmation

Pay by Bank is supported by most UK banks, including Lloyds, Halifax, Santander, Barclays and others. Currently, it is mostly used for credit card bill payments, transferring money between bank accounts with different providers, and online purchases.

View 3 Images Online shoppers have been told to 'think twice' about the new option (Image: Creative Images Lab via Getty Images)

‌



In a separate Instagram post, the MSE team explores a new option available to online shoppers on platforms such as Amazon and eBay. It explained why customers would benefit from spending a few extra moments to enter their card details when shopping online.

It claimed: "Section 75 protects you when you buy something that costs between £100 and £30,000 using a credit card. If there's a problem with what you've bought, for example, it's broken or doesn't arrive at all, then your credit card company has a legal responsibility to come to the rescue. It's extremely powerful - there's a reason we call it your financial superhero.

"Chargeback is another way to get your money back if a retailer refuses to refund you. Unlike Section 75, you can use it if you paid with a debit card as well as a credit card, and it works for spends under £100."

‌



View 3 Images eBay and Amazon are two of the bigger retailers that offer this payment method (Image: Getty Images)

While this new method typically speeds up the online checkout process for most shoppers, it's crucial to understand there's a catch. Consumers who run into problems might find it harder to recover their funds if things don't go to plan.

The MSE website reported: "With Pay by Bank, all you have are the retailer's own policies and your normal consumer rights – and enforcing these can be tricky if the retailer won't play ball or has gone bust. This means that if something goes wrong with a Pay by Bank purchase, you're essentially on your own.

News.title: How Donald Trump could retain power after leaving office – 'It gives me shivers'
News.content:
How Donald Trump could retain power after leaving office – 'It gives me shivers'

An author who has written four books about the US president has revealed how he believes Donald Trump could retain power and access to the White House even once he leaves office

View 3 Images Trump may want to cling to some power long after he leaves office, an author has claimed (Image: Daniel Heuer/UPI/Shutterstock)

Donald Trump's current term in office is due to end in January 2029 - but one author warns he could still cling to power.

‌



Journalist Michael Wolff, who has written four books about Donald Trump including 'Fire and Fury' about the POTUS' first term, has claimed Trump could retain power once his second administration comes to an end.

‌



The US constitution states no person can be elected president more than twice, but that hasn't stopped 79-year-old Trump from teasing he could try to run again anyway after 'Trump 2028' MAGA-style red caps emerged. In a previous interview, Trump told NBC there "are methods which you could do it", before adding: "I'm not joking.. a lot of people want me to do it".

‌



View 3 Images Trump's second term is due to come to an end in 2029 (Image: AP)

Wolff revealed during a podcast episode on The Daily Beast how Trump could at least keep some influence in the Oval Office - through the use of his own children.

In the new episode of 'Inside Trump's Head', the journalist said Trump's oldest son, Donald Trump Jr, could be his method for keeping a foot in the door.

‌



"He has spent his life as his father's lackey," Wolff noted of Donald Jr. "He's spent his life in a business that is of very little consequence except to support his father, who gives me the shivers."

View 3 Images He could keep power through his eldest son, Donald Trump Jr, according to Wolff (Image: YONHAP/EPA-EFE/REX/Shutterstock)

The writer went on to say Donald Jr. seems the most likely successor since Trump's other offspring such as Ivanka and Tiffany have essentially "taken themselves out of the running". Lara Trump, the wife of Trump's third child Eric Trump, said in a podcast that she would consider running for office again if the circumstances were right.

Article continues below

The insight comes as Trump continues to wage his war with Iran, causing friction with many NATO allies. His decisions over the Strait of Hormuz in particular have prompted widespread condemnation from global leaders, with jet fuel shortages and an ever-increasing cost of gas and oil being felt across the world. The war could mean Trump may depart the Oval Office in two years' time with a long list of fraught relationships.

Wolff said Trump will require some influence over the White House when he retires if he is to retain power - or he may even turn on the Republican Party.

"He really enjoyed that in his Mar-A-Lago interregnum," Wolff said. "So, he goes back to that still with the Republicans coming to kiss his rings, with his pronouncements being the leading Republican pronouncements, still being able to rag on whatever Democrat is in the White House and then, at some point, he dies a happy man... However, he would be much less happy if someone in the Republican Party replaced him."

News.title: Iran war to 'trigger 150,000 UK job losses and cost average family £730'
News.content:
Iran war to 'trigger 150,000 UK job losses and cost average family £730'

A former Bank of England rate-setter has spelt out the potential impact of the Middle East conflict on workers and household budgets

View 2 Images Critics say US President Donald Trump is harming UK households through what has been dubbed "Trumpflation" (Image: Pool/ABACA/Shutterstock)

The Iran war could trigger 150,000 UK job losses and cost the average households £730, experts have warned. An economic downturn caused by the Middle East conflict is forecast to hammer the UK’s already go-slow growth this year and next.

‌



Consultants Oxford Economics predicts the hit to firms will mean unemployment grows by 0.5%, or the equivalent of 150,000 jobs. It also warns that inflation will jump to 4.5% last year, up from the 3.3% it reached in March as confirmed by the Office for National Statistics. The jump on the scale is much more than the 3.5% peak forecast by the Bank of England and a number of other economists.

‌



Michael Saunders, senior advisor at Oxford Economics and a former rate-setter at the Bank of England, said: “Even if the war ended very soon, the outlook for the economy is pretty grim.”

‌



He also warned about the impact on household budgets from soaring fuel and other costs.

“The average household will be about £730 a year worse off than we expected at the start of this year,” Mr Saunders told an event organised by think tank the Resolution Foundation. “Of course, it could be worse if the war goes on for longer.”

‌



View 2 Images Former Bank of England rate-setter Michael Saunders says prospects for UK economy are "grim" (Image: PA)

McDonald's set to raise UK prices due to an Iran war cost shock READ MORE :

The concern is around both the immediate impact of the conflict, in terms of higher energy costs and the like, as well as what are called the secondary effects, for instance workers demanding higher wages to offset what they fear will be increasing inflation.

If is this prospect of people’s expectations of higher inflation that the Bank of England will have on its mind when its Monetary Policy Committee meets next Thursday to decide whether to change its base rate, currently at 3.75%.

Article continues below

Mr Saunders predicted the Bank may increase rates to 4.25% later this year, especially if, as it forecasts, inflation reaches 4% by July.

However, other economists are far less certain the Bank will press ahead with any increases. Liz Martins, senior UK economist at HSBC, told the same event she thought inflation was still only likely to rise to around 3.5%.

It came as the Resolution Foundation says an energy shock caused by the Middle East war will cost UK households a combined £11billion this year.

News.title: Prince Harry quietly marks Queen Elizabeth’s 100th birthday with moving gesture
News.content:
Prince Harry quietly marks Queen Elizabeth’s 100th birthday with moving gesture

The Duke of Sussex has honoured his late grandmother on the 100th anniversary on her birthday by sending flowers to her Windsor grave site

View 4 Images Prince Harry found a way to honour his late grandmother on what would've been her 100th birthday, despite living thousands of miles away (Image: Getty Images)

Prince Harry has privately marked the 100th anniversary of Queen Elizabeth’s birth with a moving gesture, despite living thousands of miles away. The Duke of Sussex honoured his late grandmother by sending a large bouquet of flowers to her burial site in Windsor Castle.

‌



During Harry’s occasional trips back to the UK after he quit his royal role in 2020, he has often travelled to Windsor to pay his respects to the late Queen, who he was said to have a strong relationship with. Throughout his childhood and early adulthood, the Duke of Sussex was close with his grandmother, however their relationship was said to have soured after Harry quit the Firm.

‌



View 4 Images Prince Harry sent flowers to Queen Elizabeth's grace to mark her 100th birthday

‌



In 2023, on the first anniversary of her passing, Harry made a quiet visit to the chapel while in the UK, paying his respects away from the public eye. Two years later, he again visited her grave during a return home, marking the third anniversary of her death with another personal moment of reflection.

While Harry marked his late grandmother’s centenary in private, the Royal Family stepped out for a series of events. The day began with King Charles paying a heartfelt tribute to his 'darling mama' in a moving video message, describing how "she remained constant, steadfast and wholly devoted to the people she served".

The King and Queen Camilla then joined other senior royals to view the design recommendations for the Queen Elizabeth Memorial at the British Museum, while Princess Anne officially opened The Queen Elizabeth II Garden in The Regent’s Park in London.

‌



Afterwards, the Prince and Princess of Wales joined other senior members of the Firm for a reception at Buckingham Palace with charities and organisations associated with the late Queen, as well as some of the UK’s oldest citizens who were also celebrating their 100th birthday on April 21.

View 4 Images Harry has honoured his late grandmother on many of his trips back to the UK since 2020 (Image: Getty Images)

After the late Queen’s death in 2022, Harry and his wife Meghan Markle travelled to the UK for her funeral, with Harry sharing an emotional tribute to grandmother in the days after her passing.

‌



At the time, he wrote: "In celebrating the life of my grandmother, Her Majesty The Queen — and in mourning her loss — we are all reminded of the guiding compass she was to so many in her commitment to service and duty. She was globally admired and respected.

“Her unwavering grace and dignity remained true throughout her life and now her everlasting legacy. Let us echo the words she spoke after the passing of her husband, Prince Philip, words which can bring comfort to all of us now: 'Life, of course, consists of final partings as well as first meetings.' "

View 4 Images The Royal Family hosted a reception at Buckingham Palace to mark the anniversary (Image: Aaron Chown/PA Wire)

‌



"Granny, while this final parting brings us great sadness, I am forever grateful for all of our first meetings — from my earliest childhood memories with you, to meeting you for the first time as my Commander-in-Chief, to the first moment you met my darling wife and hugged your beloved great-grandchildren."

He continued. "I cherish these times shared with you, and the many other special moments in between. You are already sorely missed, not just by us, but by the world over.”

Article continues below

The late Queen is buried at the King George VI Memorial Chapel with her husband of 73 years, Prince Philip, who died in 2021. Also buried in the historic chapel are her parents, King George VI, who died in 1952, and the Queen Mother, who died in 2002, as well as her sister, Princess Margaret, who passed away the same year.

News.title: Anyone with summer 2026 holidays booked warned 'keep all receipts' in new alert
News.content:
Anyone with summer 2026 holidays booked warned 'keep all receipts' in new alert

Travel insurance specialist has issued advice, as cancellations and delays may happen

View 3 Images Holiday-goers urged to take out travel insurance before going away (Image: Getty)

As airlines continue to navigate fuel supply challenges caused by the Middle East conflict, some flights may be disrupted, or fares may increase. Some energy bosses have claimed Europe only has six weeks' worth of jet fuel left. Tom Vaughan, a travel insurance specialist at Confused.com, has offered advice for passengers with summer holidays coming up.

‌



He also warned that cancellations and delays may happen, and stressed the importance of preparing in advance and knowing what to do if a trip is axed. "For Brits planning to travel this summer, it’s worth being aware that flight cancellations and delays could happen as airlines respond to operational pressures," he said.

‌



"Disruptions like this can leave travellers unsure about their rights and what steps to take next if they are affected. The good news is that UK passengers have rights if their flight is cancelled.

‌



"Airlines should offer a refund or an alternative flight, even if your ticket was non-refundable." If passengers do experience disruption, Tom has shared some steps to follow.

Firstly, he says travellers should contact their airline as soon as possible to confirm their options, including rebooking or a refund. He also recommends: "Keep receipts for any essential costs like food, accommodation or transport, as these may be reimbursed".

View 3 Images Passengers have been urged to keep their receipts

‌



Tom said passengers may still be entitled to assistance (such as meals or a hotel stay) while waiting for a new flight. "If you booked a package holiday, check if it’s ATOL protected and contact your travel provider for support", he added.

The travel insurance specialist went on to say that people who pay by credit card "may have additional protection if things don’t go to plan". Lastly, he urged people to review their travel insurance policy and speak to their insurer to understand what extra costs they could claim back.

He also says it is "always sensible" to take out travel insurance before going away. "Even if you are able to claim directly via the airline, an insurer can guide you on how to make a claim," he explained.

‌



Tom continued: "With the right policy in place, you may also be able to claim back for other parts of your holiday that were affected as a result. If you've recently experienced flight cancellations, our flight compensation guide will help to break down your options."

View 3 Images Tom says airlines should offer a refund or an alternative flight, even if your ticket was non-refundable

Inflation climbed higher last month as the knock-on effects from the Iran war started to hit the cost of living for UK households. The Office for National Statistics reported an annual rate of Consumer Prices Index (CPI) inflation of 3.3% for March, increasing from 3% last month.

‌



It meant inflation picked up to its highest level since December, with higher fuel prices a significant driver. The ONS indicated that fuel prices were the main area where the impact of the Iran conflict had already been reflected in their data.

While jet fuel costs have risen, the ONS said that air fares are based on previously booked flights, meaning that the March data was not yet impacted by inflation linked to the conflict. This means airfare inflation is likely to continue rising this year as higher jet fuel costs are passed on to passengers.

‌



KLM has made several adjustments to its flight schedule for the coming month. The airline says: "This concerns a limited number of flights within Europe that, due to rising kerosene costs, are currently no longer financially viable to operate. There is no kerosene shortage. KLM will operate 80 fewer return flights to and from Schiphol, which is less than 1% of its European flights during that period.

"Passengers affected by these changes will be rebooked onto the next available flight. As these are destinations KLM serves multiple times a day — such as London and Düsseldorf — travellers can usually be accommodated quickly. KLM expects a busy May holiday period and is making sure passengers can travel to their holiday destinations as planned."

In a new statement, Lufthansa has said: "The Lufthansa Group has secured (“hedged”) approximately 80 per cent of its kerosene requirements for 2026 and approximately 40 per cent for 2027 based, among other things, on the price of crude oil - both at pre-crisis price levels. With this level of hedging, we are in a better position than most competitors."

Article continues below

Meanwhile, easyJet has said it is not currently seeing any disruption to flights and doesn’t plan to make any changes to its flight schedule.

There’s a particular moment, somewhere between the first warm evening and the smell of charcoal catching, when cooking moves outside and everything feels a little more relaxed. Alfresco dining, at its best, isn’t about precision or performance – it’s about generosity, ease and the quiet theatre of food shared in the open air. This spring, as longer days pull us into gardens, balconies and borrowed patches of sun, it’s less about what’s on the table and more about how it brings people together.

That’s the thinking behind this collection of recipes, created in collaboration with Elevated Food For Life, Laura James and chef and food consultant Jason Shaw. His approach is refreshingly unfussy: “When I cook outdoors, I always think about balance… a great alfresco table usually has a mix of textures, temperatures and flavours – something smoky, fresh, creamy and crunchy.” It’s a philosophy that runs through everything here, from slow-cooked lamb neck with charred leeks and burrata to quick, bright dishes designed for last-minute gatherings.

Crucially, these are recipes that understand the mood of outdoor cooking. “I always recommend dishes that are simple to cook over flame but still feel generous and impressive when you serve them outdoors,” Shaw says. “Cooking over charcoal adds depth to ingredients that might otherwise feel quite simple.” That might mean a spatchcock chicken marinated with garlic, herbs and lemon for a hit of Mediterranean freshness, or salmon paired with charred baby gem – the sort of detail that quietly elevates a dish without overcomplicating it.

Even the more comforting elements have their place here. Think filled potato skins loaded with macaroni cheese, designed to be prepped ahead and passed around as the evening cools, or a prawn saganaki that feels both rustic and quietly showy. And yes, dessert belongs on the barbecue too: grilled apricots, their sweetness intensified by the heat, finished simply with cream or yoghurt.

For more spontaneous moments, Shaw leans on instinct over instruction. “The best impromptu outdoor meals rely on great ingredients and simple preparation rather than complex cooking,” he says – whether that’s a quick carpaccio, a watermelon and feta salad, or flatbreads thrown on the grill and torn apart at the table.

If there’s a single takeaway, it’s this: the smallest details often matter most. “One of the simplest things people can do to elevate outdoor cooking is focus on the finishing touches,” Shaw explains. A squeeze of citrus, a scatter of fresh herbs, a final drizzle of good olive oil – small gestures that turn something good into something memorable.

Because ultimately, alfresco dining isn’t about perfection. It’s about the easy rhythm of cooking, eating and lingering a little longer than planned – preferably with something smoky on the plate and a glass in hand.

Six easy al fresco recipe ideas

BBQ lamb neck with leeks and burrata

open image in gallery An underrated cut turned showstopper – slow, smoky lamb with creamy burrata to balance ( Elevated Food For Life/Laura James )

In this recipe, we are grilling lamb neck, a fabulously underrated and inexpensive cut of lamb that is high in protein and low in fat once grilled. Ordinarily, a tough, hard-working muscle that requires slow cooking, lamb lends itself remarkably well to the BBQ.

We are serving it with chargrilled heart-healthy leeks and tender burrata, a high-protein Italian cow’s milk cheese made from mozzarella and cream.

The recipe is low on ingredients; in fact, it couldn’t be easier to cook, but look after this and treat it with respect, and you’ll get more wow from your grill than you ever could with a burger and sausages.

Serves: 2

Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:

300g lamb neck (2 pieces)

2 leeks

100g burrata cheese

2 stalks of rosemary or oregano

Method

1. Light your BBQ and allow the charcoal to stop flaming and turn white.

2. Season your lamb neck steaks with salt and place them on the grill with a sprig of herb on each.

3. Cook for around 15-20 minutes in total, turning frequently to even out the cooking.

4. Remove the lamb and allow to rest for a further 15 minutes.

5. In the meantime, add your leeks with the outer skin on to the slightly cooler charcoals or embers to the side.

6. The leeks will be done when you prick them with a knife, try to lift them and if they fall off the knife, they are done.

7. Thinly slice the lamb onto a plate, split the leeks in half (you only eat the inner, tender part).

BBQ spatchcock chicken

open image in gallery Flattened for even cooking, crisp skin and maximum flavour from the grill ( Elevated Food For Life/Laura James )

Rather than running the risk of grabbing some cheap chicken breasts that will only toughen up on the grill, in this recipe, we’re grilling a young chicken (also known as a poussin), spatchcocking it and grilling it with heart-healthy leeks for an amazingly tender dish.

Serves: 2

Time: 40 minutes

Ingredients:

1 young chicken (poussin)

2 shallots

2 tbsp Elevated house rub

1tsp rapeseed oil

100g/4oz Elevated BBQ sauce

Method:

1. Either get your butcher to spatchcock the poussin, or remove the backbone with a sharp paring knife. This allows it to be spread out and cook better and more evenly on the grill.

2. Rub the bird all over with our house rub loosened with a little oil and allow to stand for an hour or so before cooking (overnight is even better).

3. Light your BBQ and allow the charcoal to stop flaming and turn white.

4. Using either two cooling racks with which to sandwich the bird, or a pair of skewers going through it at a cross angle, place it on the grill skin side down.

5. Flip after 5 minutes and continue to turn (for extra flavour, place some sprigs of herbs under the bird as it cooks).

6. Meanwhile, clean and split your shallots and gentle char grill alongside the chicken.

7. Using a meat thermometer, ensure the chicken is cooked to higher than 75C in the thickest parts.

8. When done, remove and allow to stand for 20 minutes.

9. Serve with the chargrilled shallots and either our BBQ sauce or a good store-bought one.

BBQ salmon

open image in gallery Proof that simple wins – smoky salmon and charred greens doing all the work ( Elevated Food For Life/Laura James )

You don’t have to buy low-cost burgers and sausages to keep your BBQ costs down. In this recipe, we take salmon tail fillet, a cheaper cook and let it cook over charcoals, serving alongside char-grilled lettuce, which tastes a little like ‘seaweed’ from a Chinese restaurant.

You don’t have to buy low-cost burgers and sausages to keep your BBQ costs down.

In this recipe, we take salmon tail fillet, a cheaper cut and let it cook over charcoals, serving alongside char-grilled lettuce, which tastes a little like “seaweed” from a Chinese restaurant.

The baby gem brings with it fibre, antioxidants, vitamins A and K, and minerals such as calcium, potassium, and iron, which help with muscle function, bone strength and oxygen transport.

Serves: 2

Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:

360g/12oz salmon tail fillet (two pieces)

2 lemons

1 baby gem or 1 small romaine lettuce

Method:

1. Light your BBQ and allow the charcoal to stop flaming and turn white.

2. Season the salmon with salt and place it on the grill skin-side down with a sprig of basil on top.

3. Cover with an inverted frying pan so the top can steam through.

4. Half the lettuce and place it on the grill, centre-side down.

5. Half the lemon and add to the grill, cut side down.

6. After around 8 minutes, check that the salmon is done.

7. Serve with the grilled lettuce and lemon wedge.

Ultimate creamy mashed potatoes

open image in gallery Comfort food still has a place outside – rich, silky mash for cooler evenings ( Elevated Food For Life/Laura James )

Here’s an indulgent side dish recipe for those days when you want something familiar and comforting when the chills set in.

It’s Jason’s ultimate mashed potatoes recipe, using only the best ingredients: potatoes, our own organic butter and double cream. We won’t pretend this one is super health-giving, but this is a dish that just makes you feel warm inside.

We prepare the potatoes in the same way Italian chefs do for the base of gnocchi. By baking the potatoes, we are not diluting the vitamin and mineral content with steam or water and keeping the dish as nutritious as possible.

Serves: 4

Time: 1 hour 15 minutes

Ingredients:

600g/21oz (around four) large floury potatoes such as Cara, Maris Piper or King Edwards

150g/5oz organic double cream

50g/1.8oz organic butter

Salt and pepper to taste

Method:

1. Pre-heat the oven to 200C/390F (fan) or 220C/430F (convection).

2. Place the potatoes on an oven-proof tray and drizzle with a little olive oil and sea salt.

3. Agitate the potatoes to cover with the oil and salt.

4. Place in the oven until cooked (around 60 minutes depending on size).

5. Working quickly with a cloth to avoid burning, split each potato and scoop out the warm, tender flesh. Reserve the skins to either return to the oven and crisp up as a snack.

6. Pass all the flesh through a sieve to create the ultimate smooth, intense pomme puree.

7. Add the cream and butter to a pan and heat until it reduces to a custard consistency.

8. Fold in the potato to the emulsion and add salt and pepper to taste.

Prawn saganaki

open image in gallery Quick, punchy and built for sharing – the kind of dish that disappears fast ( Elevated Food For Life/Laura James )

Quick, simple, and super tasty, this recipe is super high in protein and omega-3 fats while retaining a real show-stopping look when served at the table, especially if steaming in the pot.

Saganaki comes from a Greek dish, rediscovered by us on our trip to Athens and Sparta in September 2023, when James ran Spartathlon, and Jason crewed for him. The name comes from the double-handed pot in which it is traditionally cooked, but essentially it’s a form of sauteeing or shallow frying. We ate this dish in several iterations, and they were all delicious.

Raw shrimp or tiger prawns are essential here, either peeled and deveined, or left in shells for a more rustic look and eaten, with all the juices kept intact.

The ingredients naturally carry salt and saline notes, so we have consciously not added any more to the recipe and the spiced heat that gives it a zing comes from the chilli, so no black pepper either.

Serves: 1

Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:

6-10 (75g/2.6oz) raw peeled shrimp/tiger prawns

1/4 red chilli de-seeded and diced

3-4 spring onions, thinly sliced

150g/5oz BB Tomato Fondue

5-6 pitted black olives cut into quarters

3-4 cherry tomatoes cut into quarters

5tsp feta cheese

2tsp Olive oil

Squeeze lemon juice

Crusty sourdough to serve

Method:

1. Pre-make your BB Tomato Fondue or draw some from the refrigerator or freezer.

2. Pre-heat the oven to 180C/360F (fan) or 200C/390F (convection).

3. Heat your skillet/pan on the stove top, add a splash of olive oil and seal off the prawns quickly on both sides, lifting out and reserving one side (these are not fully cooked yet).

4. While the skillet is still hot, add the chilli and the white slices of the spring onion, cooking out for 1-2 minutes but not colouring.

5. Add the Tomato Fondue, stir and bring to a gentle bubble.

6. Place the tomato and olive quarters on top, cover with a butter wrapper as a cartouche and pop in the oven for 5-6 minutes until thoroughly heated through.

7. Remove from the oven and lay the sealed prawns on top.

8. Pop back in the oven for a further 3-4 minutes (do not cover) until the prawns have cooked through.

9. Just before serving, crumble the salty feta over the top, along with the green parts of the sliced spring onions, torn Greek basil (or thyme) and a squeeze of lemon juice.

10. Drizzle with olive oil and serve with warm, crusty sourdough.

BBQ grilled apricots and almond macaroons

open image in gallery Dessert goes on the grill – caramelised fruit and just enough sweetness to finish ( Elevated Food For Life/Laura James )

A BBQ pudding? Yes please!

In this simple dessert recipe, we harness the power of our grill to first chargrill and then stew down our stone fruits alongside some delicious blueberries and serve them with a simple almond macaroon also done on the grill.

Nutritionally, we are using just a dash of natural maple syrup here to bring out the natural flavours of the fruits. Apricots are high in antioxidants, can help promote gut health and have heart-protective properties.

We’ve married them with blueberries for both a flavour enhancement, but also as we’ve added cardamom to the cookies. Cardamom and blueberries together have been shown to help boost natural killer cells – a type of immune cell that can help fight cancer.

Serves: 6

Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:

For the fruit:

12-14 apricots

100g/4oz blueberries

Dash of maple syrup

For the macaroons:

2 egg whites

150g/5oz caster sugar

150g/5oz ground almonds

5 tsp flaked almonds

½ tsp ground cardamom

For the crème chantilly:

250ml/9oz double cream

1g ground cardamom

Splash of rum (optional)

½ tsp vanilla extract

Method:

1. Light your BBQ and allow the charcoal to stop flaming and turn white.

2. Make your dessert before you make anything else to ensure the grill is clean from meat juices.

3. Split the apricots and destone, lightly spray with oil to stop them sticking and place them flesh down first to caramelise.

4. Flip over after 2-3 minutes and cook skin side down for a further 2-3 minutes.

5. Remove to a heat-proof dish, add the blueberries and maple syrup, cover and place on a rack or cooler part of the grill to keep warm and gently stew out.

6. The macaroons can be made in advance if desired.

7. Whisk the egg whites until soft peaks are formed.

8. Fold the sugar, ground almonds and cardamom together.

9. Fold the dry mix into the eggs, being careful not to remove the air.

10. Spray a jam tart or muffin pan with a little oil, divide the mixture into 12 and place one in each receptacle.

11. Cover and place on the grill (or in the oven) for 5 minutes or so.

12. Flip and cook on the other side for a further 5 minutes.

13. Whip the double cream to peaks and add the rum, vanilla and cardamom.

14. Place the stone fruits in a serving tray and surround with the macaroons, daub with the cream to serve.

For more inspiration – from clever cooking shortcuts to thoughtfully designed pieces that make hosting that bit easier – explore Elevated and the new-in garden collection at Laura James, where alfresco dining is treated as both an art and a way of bringing people together.
